problem:
Express the Maclaurin series expansion for ${3}^{x},$
 given by

$$
{3}^{x}=1+(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)x+\frac{(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)^{2}{x}^{2}}{2!}+\frac{(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)^{3}{x}^{3}}{3!}+⋯
$$

using sigma notation.
worked_solution:
The first four terms of the series are

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =1 \\ {a}_{1} & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)x \\ {a}_{2} & =\frac{(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)^{2}{x}^{2}}{2!} \\ {a}_{3} & =\frac{(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)^{3}{x}^{3}}{3!}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we can express these terms using a common format, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)^{0}{x}^{0}}{0!} \\ {a}_{1} & =\frac{(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)^{1}{x}^{1}}{1!} \\ {a}_{2} & =\frac{(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)^{2}{x}^{2}}{2!} \\ {a}_{3} & =\frac{(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)^{3}{x}^{3}}{3!}.\end{aligned}
$$

We deduce that the general formula for the $n$th term is

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)^{n}{x}^{n}}{n!}\,.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{3}^{x}={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }\frac{(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)^{n}{x}^{n}}{n!}\,.
$$
